commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 entries with an optional `:port` suffix; when either side
carries a port, both suffixes must match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling:
The defect is an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) in the IPv6 known-host matching added by ab9fcd9, and it is only reachable through the composition of the two edited commits; neither edit alone can produce it.

Commit 1 (ab9fcd9, 'knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals', edited): the edited version of knownhost_ipv6_part() accepts bracketed entries with an OPTIONAL port suffix -- it drops the original requirements that ']' be followed by ':' and a non-empty numeric port, and scans the port from close+1, skipping one optional ':'. On its own this is purely a permissive feature change (the default-port form '[::1]' that OpenSSH writes is now accepted): the returned *suffix is still close+1, which is always at most the NUL terminator of the NUL-terminated host string, so every string the matcher reads stays in bounds. Verified: with only this commit edited, the probe returns LIBSSH2_KNOWNHOST_CHECK_NOTFOUND and exits 0 under ASan.

Commit 2 (c18d534, 'tidy-up: miscellaneous', edited): adds a one-line tidy-up that moves the suffix output from close+1 to close+2, i.e. past the constant ':' separator, so the matcher compares the bare port. Against the REAL ab9fcd9 this is safe: the real knownhost_ipv6_part() only accepts bracketed entries whose ']' is followed by ':' plus a non-empty validated port, so close+2 always points at a digit inside the string. Verified: with only this commit edited, the probe is also clean. The one-line diff carries no bound information of its own -- its safety is an invariant owned by the other commit.

Composition: with commit 1's relaxation in place, a stored name that ends at the ']' (e.g. the default-port entry '[::1]', heap-allocated as exactly hostlen+1 bytes by knownhost_add()) passes validation, and commit 2's close+2 then points one byte PAST the NUL terminator, i.e. one past the end of the 6-byte allocation. knownhost_plain_match() passes that pointer to strcmp(), which reads it: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1, reached from the public API via libssh2_knownhost_readline('[::1] ssh-rsa ...') + libssh2_knownhost_check("[::01]:2222", ...).

Why a correct fix is non-local: each diff is benign in its own context -- commit 1's optional-port parsing keeps every returned pointer NUL-anchored, and commit 2's +2 offset is provably in-bounds given the real commit 1's validation -- so a reviewer auditing either commit in isolation sees correct maintenance. The invariant that made close+2 safe (']' always followed by ':port') was created in one commit and consumed in the other; restoring memory safety requires reasoning about both at once (either re-anchor the suffix to the validated separator position that commit 1's parser actually found, or restore the structural validation commit 1 relaxed), not merely reverting lines visible in a single diff. Both single-edited trees and the original batch run the probe cleanly (exit 0); only the combined tree aborts under ASan (rc 134 with abort_on_error=1).
